pr_title: Skip adding WeMo device on failure
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Some WeMo devices can get into an unresponsive state where they always return a HTTP 500 status code when probing their state. When the wemo component is setup using a list of static devices, the first device to fail this way causes the remaining devices to not be setup. This PR handles an exception from WeMo devices that fail to return their current state when requested during setup. 

If the user resets the device, it will become responsive again, and the next scheduled `async_discover_and_schedule` call will cause it to be added to Home Assistant.

Traceback of the issue from https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/88602#issuecomment-1512207246

```
  File "/srv/venv_310/lib/python3.10/site-packages/homeassistant/components/wemo/__init__.py", line 152, in async_add_unique_device

  File "/srv/venv_310/lib/python3.10/site-packages/homeassistant/components/wemo/wemo_device.py", line 154, in async_register_device
    await hass.async_add_executor_job(wemo.get_state, True)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 58, in run
    result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
  File "/srv/venv_310/lib/python3.10/site-packages/pywemo/ouimeaux_device/__init__.py", line 222, in get_state
    self.update_binary_state()
  File "/srv/venv_310/lib/python3.10/site-packages/pywemo/ouimeaux_device/__init__.py", line 200, in update_binary_state
    self.basic_state_params = self.basicevent.GetBinaryState() or {}
  File "/srv/venv_310/lib/python3.10/site-packages/pywemo/ouimeaux_device/api/service.py", line 267, in __call__
    raise ActionException(msg) from last_exception
pywemo.exceptions.ActionException: Error communicating with Grow Lights after 3 attempts. Giving up.
```

Tried these remedies:
2. Remove Wemo Integration
3. Reboot HA and reinstall Wemo Integration
4. Set static IP on the device (router) and in HA configuration.yaml set static IP, reboot again.
5. Tried 'discovery: false' in yaml as well

```
wemo:
  discovery: true
  static:
    - 192.168.0.13
```

The log file displays this error:
`2023-03-14 15:55:39.167 ERROR (SyncWorker_0) [homeassistant.components.wemo] Unable to get description url for WeMo at: 192.168.0.13`

The switch can be controlled with the REST call by changing the "binary state" so something is up with the Wemo integration.
Also having this issue. Fails to automatically find devices. Setting discovery to false and providing static IPs does not resolve.

It'll help to have some additional information. If you can make a SOAP request to the device, then try these directions: https://github.com/pywemo/pywemo#if-discovery-doesnt-work-on-your-network

If the `url` can't be found with `pywemo.setup_url_for_address` try entering it manually and calling `pywemo.discovery.device_from_description`. `pywemo.discovery.device_from_description` should give some extra output that'll help track down why it's not working.

The expected device responses can be found here: https://github.com/pywemo/pywemo/tree/main/tests/vcr

Thanks for the pointers!  I dug into the pywemo bits and ultimately if you give the library a static IP the url mechanism in pywemo/ouimeaux is doing two things with your static ip:

1.  Get a hostname from your ip which can be done through the socket package
2. Call a URL:

```http://your_ip:port_range/setup.xml``` where port range is between 49153-49159.  The library tries all the ports in succession until they hit a good one.  If this GET fails, it's game over.

```http://192.168.0.20:49153/setup.xml``` or better yet from the HA terminal do this:  
```curl -X GET http://192.168.0.20:49153/setup.xml``` 
In that way you can get a sense if pywemo is going to work. 

I had a weird case where I could call POST to turn the switch on/off but pywemo's GET for setup.xml would fail.  My issue turned out be a VLAN config problem that resulted in frame losses which I was able to resolve and eventually make the curl GET call on HA terminal on port 49153.  duh, my bad.  Others likely have something else going on but they may be able to perform that simple test to narrow things down.

After taking out my static device list and setting it to discover, the other switches apear to be working fine.  When the static list was there if the first device failed to poll correctly it just didn't seem to bother trying any of the others.
```
>>> device.device_type
'Switch'
>>> device.firmware_version
'WeMo_WW_2.00.11532.PVT-OWRT-SNS'
```

This is a gen1 plug device, if it matters.  I did get everything to finally play nicely by rebooting that specific device then everything worked again.  The issue that should be looked at it is why hass stopped on the first device instead of moving on to the others.
```
>>> import pywemo
>>> url = pywemo.setup_url_for_address("10.0.0.130")
>>> print(url)
http://10.0.0.130:49153/setup.xml
>>> device = pywemo.discovery.device_from_description(url)
>>> print(device)
<WeMo Switch "Grow Lights">
>>> device.get_state()
0
```

Good data point, thanks for sharing!  I've spent a fair amount of time trying to decipher Belkin Wemo failures.  What I ended up noting was that:

1. The Belkin underlying Python library is no longer maintained (https://github.com/iancmcc/ouimeaux).
3. You can at least talk to the switch directly with an http [post](https://github.com/cayossarian/ha-node-red-wemo) to control the switch so why talk to the Belkin mother ship?  This direct access essentially says the switch has no security; I sandbox it in the router.
4. Belkin has balked on Matter support so they appear to be proprietary/cloud from now on [https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2023/03/belkin-takes-a-big-step-back-from-matter-endangering-universal-smart-home-standard/](url)

Corporate Belkin is basically saying my way or the highway...guess what, lots of highways.  I don't want a switch that insists on publishing my light status to the cloud.  I have two switches and I'll control them within my network and disable the unsupported Belkin/Wemo Integration to avoid polluting the log.  If they don't work anymore, off to the waste bin.  At least Eve switches don't have a market for my data.  I can't image HA developers spending their valuable time on Belkin given where the market is going.
